newsitem.title: OMAN: Oman sees two bln rial income, 2.26 spending in 97.
newsitem.headline: Oman sees two bln rial income, 2.26 spending in 97.

text.p: Oman's economy minister said on Wednesday the Gulf Arab state's 1997 budget forecast revenue of 2.003 billion Omani rials and spending of 2.266 billion rials.

In response to questions from the official Oman News Agency, Ahmad bin Abdul-Nabi Mekki said oil income accounted for 1.502 billion rials, gas revenue for 69 million and other income for 432 million rials.
Mekki's statement, a copy of which was obtained by Reuters, said the revenue calculations for the five-year plan to 2000 were based on a oil price of $15 per barrel.
He said the 2.266 billion rials in spending, up from 2.236 in 1996, was made up of 1.815 billion rials in current expenditures and 398 million rials for investments.

Oman, which has said it aims to balance its budget by 2000, had projected a deficit of 218 million rials in 1996. It has said the provisional deficit in 1995 was 274.3 million rials, down from 495.5 million rials in 1994. ($1=0.377 rials)
